title: Linux Quiz
description: Revisit the key ideas in Linux. Read each choice carefully. You can try the quiz again after reviewing the lessons.

questions.question: What does pwd show?
questions.explanation: A terminal displays a shell, which reads commands. pwd prints the directory you are currently using. The output is the path of your current directory. It differs between computers.

questions.question: Which option includes dot files?
questions.explanation: ls lists directory entries. The -a option includes names beginning with a dot, which are often hidden in normal views. The second list can show hidden names such as .git. Neither command changes files.

questions.question: Which command moves into a folder?
questions.explanation: mkdir creates a directory. cd changes the shell's current directory. Use a new name that does not replace existing work. The final path ends in linux-practice. This is the workspace for later examples.

questions.question: What does > do here?
options: Read the file without changing it
questions.explanation: printf writes text. A redirection sign sends that text into a file. cat prints a file's contents. The file contains two lines: Moon and Ocean. The single > creates or replaces the named file.

questions.question: Which redirection appends?
questions.explanation: Two redirection signs append text to the end of a file. Earlier content stays in place. Zoo appears after the existing lines.

questions.question: Do later edits automatically update both copies?
questions.explanation: cp makes another copy of a file. Give a new destination name when you want to preserve both versions. The copy has the same text at the moment cp ran. Later edits to one file do not automatically update the other.

questions.question: Does grep edit the matching lines?
questions.explanation: grep prints lines that match a pattern. With -F it treats the pattern as fixed text rather than a special pattern language. Matching lines containing Moon are printed. This does not edit the file.

questions.question: What does the pipe connect?
options: One command's output to another's input
questions.explanation: wc counts things such as lines. sort writes lines in order to its output. Piping connects one command's output to another. The result counts the lines produced by sort. The original books.txt remains unchanged.

questions.question: Why quote reading notes?
options: To hide it from every user
To treat it as one path
questions.explanation: Quotes keep several words together as one shell argument. This matters when a path contains spaces. The command lists one directory whose name contains a space.

questions.question: What does r mean?
questions.explanation: Permissions describe who may read, write or execute a file. ls -l shows them along with other details. The permission letters appear at the start of the listing. Read r as read, w as write and x as execute.

questions.question: What is a process?
questions.explanation: A process is a running program. ps shows information about selected processes without stopping them. The output lists processes in the current selection, with IDs and commands. The exact list depends on the system.

questions.question: Why save commands in a script?
options: To repeat a known set of steps
questions.explanation: A script saves commands so you can run them again. This one only prints a greeting and the current path. The script prints a greeting and the current directory. Using sh reads the script without needing executable permission.
